linkedin.text:
Your restaurant pays a card fee on the tips it passes to staff.
And on the sales tax it hands to the state.

Lawmakers are trying to stop that.

Illinois passed a law against it.
Banks and card groups are fighting it in court, and lawmakers have now pushed the start to July 1, 2027.

New Jersey and Pennsylvania have bills of their own.

I'm for it. A fee on money the shop never keeps is hard to defend.

But here's my unpopular take: it's the smallest part of the bill.

A quick example.
A restaurant takes $40,000 a month in card sales.
Say $8,000 of that is tax and tips.
At a 2.5% card rate, that slice costs $200 a month.
The other $32,000 costs $800.

Win the fight on tax and tips, and you still pay $9,600 a year.

The other side, from TD Cowen analyst Jaret Seiberg: "We see nothing unique about taxes or tips."

He's right, in a way he didn't intend. If the fee is wrong on the tip, why is it right on the meal?

As a nurse, I learned to treat the cause, not just the symptom.
The fee itself is the cause. That's why I started SVPay, so shops can take payments without it.

Owners: what share of your card sales is tax and tips?

(Example only: a 2.5% all-in rate, with 20% of card sales being tax and tips.)

#SmallBusiness #Restaurants #Payments
